The '''2025–26 [[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]] season''' was the club's [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|127th season in existence]] and their [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|95th consecutive season]] in the top flight. In addition to the [[2025–26 La Liga|domestic league]], Barcelona participated in this season's editions of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] (entering for the [[FC Barcelona in international football#European Cup / Champions League|22nd consecutive season]]), reaching the quarter-finals. They also played in the [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], where they were eliminated in the semi-finals, and the [[2026 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], which they won. The season covered the period from 1 July 2025 until 30 June 2026.

Barcelona had planned to return to their historic home, the [[Camp Nou]], on 10 August 2025, following two full seasons away while the stadium underwent renovation and expansion.<ref>{{cite news |date=9 June 2025 |title=LaLiga marca el retorno al Spotify Camp Nou |trans-title=La Liga marks its return to Spotify Camp Nou |language=es |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20250609/1002479943/laliga-marca-retorno-spotify-camp-nou.html |access-date=10 June 2025 |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |archive-date=6 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260806140707/https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20250609/1002479943/laliga-marca-retorno-spotify-camp-nou.html |url-status=live}}</ref> However, delays in obtaining an occupancy licence postponed the reopening, and the club eventually played their first match back at the stadium on 22 November 2025.

Barcelona retained the La Liga title on 10 May 2026, securing their 29th league championship with a victory over [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in [[El Clásico|Clásico]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78qwgnn3vgt |title=Barcelona 2 Real Madrid 0 |date=10 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=11 May 2026 |archive-date=10 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260510222900/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78qwgnn3vgt |url-status=live}}</ref> It was the first time in the club's history that they had clinched the title by defeating their rivals. Barcelona ended the league season with 19 out of 19 wins on home soil, becoming the first Spanish team in 40 years to complete a clean sweep at home and the first to do it under the 38 game format.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/748508 |title=Raphinha at the double to ensure Barcelona's perfect LaLiga home record |publisher=ESPN |date=17 May 2026 |access-date=17 May 2026 |archive-date=18 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518054937/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/748508 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Season overview==

===Pre-season===
On 3 June, Barcelona confirmed the departure of [[Álex Valle]] to [[Como 1907|Como]] for €6 million.<ref name="Valle"/> Six days later, [[Clément Lenglet]] left the club following the termination of his contract,<ref name="Lenglet"/> subsequently joining [[Atlético Madrid]].

On 16 June, Barcelona announced their pre-season tour in [[Japan]] and [[South Korea]], respectively, with three friendly matches. In Japan, against [[Vissel Kobe]] in [[Kobe]] on 27 July; in South Korea, against [[FC Seoul]] in [[Seoul]] on 31 July, and [[Daegu FC]] in [[Daegu]] on 4 August.<ref name="Pre-season1">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4286933/fc-barcelona-to-go-to-asia-for-the-first-time-in-six-years-for-202526-preseason|title=FC Barcelona to go to Asia for the first time in six years for 2025/26 preseason|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=16 June 2025|access-date=16 June 2025|archive-date=16 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616094846/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4286933/fc-barcelona-to-go-to-asia-for-the-first-time-in-six-years-for-202526-preseason|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 June, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Joan Garcia]] from [[Derbi Barceloní|local rival]] [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] by activating the release clause of €25 million, and signing the player to a six-year contract.<ref name="JoanGarcia"/> Two days later, [[Aleix Garrido]] departed for [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] on a free transfer.<ref name="Garrido"/>

On 30 June, [[Sergi Domínguez]] was sold to [[Dinamo Zagreb]] for €1.2 million.<ref name="Domínguez"/> The following day, Barcelona loaned [[Ander Astralaga]] and [[Ansu Fati]] to [[Granada CF|Granada]] and [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] respectively.<ref name="Astralaga"/> <ref name="Fati"/> [[Noah Darvich]] departed for [[VfB Stuttgart|Stuttgart]] for €2.2 million,<ref name="Darvich"/> while [[Pau Prim]] left on a free transfer to [[Al Sadd SC|Al Sadd]].<ref name="Prim"/>

On 14 July, Barcelona signed [[Sweden men's national football team|Swedish]] winger [[Roony Bardghji]] from [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] on a four-year contract for €2.5 million with performance-based add-ons.<ref name="Roony"/><ref>{{cite web |last=Marsden |first=Sam |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45688362/barcelona-transfers-roony-bardghji-joins-fc-copenhagen |title=Barcelona transfers: Roony Bardghji joins from FC Copenhagen |work=ESPN |date=14 July 2025 |access-date=17 June 2026 |archive-date=29 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251029105709/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45688362/barcelona-transfers-roony-bardghji-joins-fc-copenhagen |url-status=live }}</ref> On the same day, [[Pablo Torre (footballer)|Pablo Torre]] was sold to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] for €5 million.<ref name="Torre"/> The next day, goalkeeper [[Áron Yaakobishvili]] was loaned to [[FC Andorra|Andorra]] for the season.<ref name="Yaakobishvili"/>

On 23 July, Barcelona secured the season-long loan of [[England national football team|English international]] forward [[Marcus Rashford]] from [[Manchester united F.C.|Manchester United]]. The deal includes an option to purchase the player at the end of the season.<ref name="Rashford"/> Two days later, [[Pau Víctor]] left for [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] for €12 million.<ref name="Víctor"/>

On 27 July, Barcelona opened their pre-season tour with a 1–3 win away against Vissel Kobe, with goals from [[Eric García (footballer, born 2001)|Eric García]], Roony Bardghji, and [[Dro Fernández]]. Four days later, Barcelona thrashed FC Seoul 3–7, with a brace apiece from [[Lamine Yamal]] and [[Ferran Torres]], and further goals from [[Robert Lewandowski]], [[Andreas Christensen]], and [[Gavi (footballer)|Gavi]].

===August===
On 4 August, Barcelona closed out their [[Asia]] tour with a 0–5 win over Daegu FC, with a brace from Gavi and goals from Lewandowski, Dro Fernández, and Marcus Rashford. Three days later, Barcelona announced the temporary suspension as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of goalkeeper [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] as a result of opening disciplinary proceedings against the player. [[Ronald Araújo]] assumed the role during this period.<ref name="Ter Stegen">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4335921/fc-barcelona-official-statement|title=Barcelona remove ter Stegen as captain.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=7 August 2025|access-date=7 August 2025|archive-date=7 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250807180712/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4335921/fc-barcelona-official-statement|url-status=live}}</ref> The player was suspended as a result of his refusal to sign a consent form for his medical data to be sent to [[La Liga]]. Ter Stegen rectified his decision the next day, 8 August, and the club reinstated him as captain.<ref name="Ter Stegen reinstated">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4336855/fc-barcelona-statement|title=Barcelona reinstate ter Stegen as captain.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=8 August 2025|access-date=11 August 2025|archive-date=9 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809183628/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4336855/fc-barcelona-statement|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 9 August, [[Iñigo Martínez]] left the club on a free transfer to join [[Al-Nassr]].<ref name="Iñigo"/> The next day, Barcelona celebrated the [[Joan Gamper Trophy]] at the [[Johan Cruyff Stadium]] to inaugurate their 2025–26 season. They faced off against [[Serie A|Italian]] club Como, winning 5–0 with goals from [[Fermin Lopez]] (2), [[Raphinha]], and Lamine Yamal (2).

On 15 August, [[Francisco Trincão]] was sold to [[Sporting CP]] for €11 million.<ref name="Trincão"/> The following day, Barcelona began their LaLiga title defense with a 0–3 away victory over Mallorca, with goals from Ferran Torres, Raphinha, and Lamine Yamal. The match saw first-team debuts for Joan Garcia, [[Jofre Torrents]], and Marcus Rashford.

On 23 August, Barcelona managed to come from 2–0 down to secure a 2–3 win away at [[Levante UD]] thanks to goals from [[Pedri]] and Ferran Torres and a last-minute own goal by [[Unai Elgezabal]]. Four days later, goalkeeper [[Iñaki Peña]] was loaned to [[Elche CF|Elche]] for the season.<ref name="Peña"/>

On 28 August, [[Jan Virgili]] departed for Mallorca for €3 million.<ref name="Virgili"/> Two days later, Barcelona were held to a 1–1 draw by [[Rayo Vallecano]] at the [[Vallecas Stadium]], with Lamine Yamal converting from the penalty spot.

===September===
On 1 September, defender [[Héctor Fort]] was loaned to Elche for the season.<ref name="Fort"/> Four days later, [[Oriol Romeu]] left the club following the termination of his contract,<ref name="Romeu"/> subsequently joining [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].

On 14 September, Barcelona marked their first home game of the season with a 6–0 demolition of [[Valencia]] at the [[Johan Cruyff Stadium|Estadi Johan Cruyff]] courtesy of braces from Fermín, Raphinha, and Robert Lewandowski. The match saw Roony Bardghji make his first-team debut. Four days later, the Blaugrana got off to a winning start in their [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League league phase |Champions League league phase]] campaign in a 1–2 away win over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] via a brace by Marcus Rashford — his first goals for the club.

On 21 September, a brace from Torres and a goal by [[Dani Olmo]] handed Barcelona a 3–0 home victory over [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] in the league. Four days later, Barcelona defeated newly-promoted side [[Real Oviedo]] 1–3, with Eric García, Lewandowski, and Araújo finding the net. Barça then capped off the month with a 2–1 home victory over [[Real Sociedad]] at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]] with goals from [[Jules Koundé]] and Lewandowski. The match saw Dro Fernández make his first-team debut.

===October===
The month of October began poorly for Barça as the Catalan club suffered their first loss of the season on 1 October in a 1–2 home loss to defending Champions League holders [[Paris Saint-Germain]] despite an early goal from Ferran Torres. Rashford's debut league goal was rendered moot in a heavy 4–1 loss away at [[Sevilla F.C.|Sevilla]] four days later.

On 18 October, goals from Pedri and a last-minute winner by Araújo secured a 2–1 league win over Catalan rivals [[Girona FC]] in a dramatic match that saw Barça boss [[Hansi Flick]] sent off in injury time. Three days later, Barcelona steamrolled past [[Olympiacos]] 6–1 at home. Fermín scored his first career hat-trick assisted by Lamine Yamal, Roony Bardghji and Dro Fernández, with the other goals scored by Lamine Yamal and Rashford (2).

On 26 October, a Fermín equaliser was not enough to get Barcelona over the line in a 2–1 away loss against [[Real Madrid]], handing the Catalans their first [[El Clásico]] loss since April 2024.

===November===
FC Barcelona’s November 2025 campaign began with a 3–1 domestic victory over Elche on November 2, followed shortly by a frustrating 3–3 draw against [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] in the Champions League on November 5. 

The team quickly regained momentum in La Liga with a 2–4 win away at Celta Vigo on November 9, leading into the most significant moment of the month: the historic reopening of the [[Camp Nou|Spotify Camp Nou]] on November 22, where the squad celebrated their return with a dominant 4–0 thrashing of [[Athletic Bilbao]]. This high point was tempered by a difficult 3–0 Champions League defeat to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on November 25, during which a first-half Araújo red card crippled their tactical approach. Ultimately, Barcelona salvaged their domestic consistency before the month closed, securing a final 3–1 victory over [[Deportivo Alavés]] on November 29 to maintain their perfect league record throughout the period.

===December===
Barcelona had a great month in December, winning all their games across [[La Liga]], the [[UEFA Champions League]] and the [[Copa del Rey|Copa Del Rey]]. The run began with a 3–1 victory over [[Atlético Madrid|Atletico Madrid]] at the Spotify Camp Nou on December 2nd with goals coming from Raphinha, Dani Olmo and Torres. This was followed by a thrilling 3–5 away win over Real Betis on December 6 with a hat trick from Torres and goals from Lamine and Roony Bardghji, the latter his first for the club.   

The team then defeated [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] 2–1 in the Champions League with a brilliant brace from Kounde, before returning to La Liga to defeat [[CA Osasuna]] 2–0 with a brace from Raphinha. Then Barcelona started their Copa del rey campaign win 0–2 victory over [[CD Guadalajara (Spain)|CD Guadalajara]] with goals coming from Rashford and Christensen each on December 16 sending them through to the Round of 16 and closing the year with 0–2 away win over [[Villarreal CF|Villareal]] on December 21 to maintain their top position of the La Liga table.

===January===
On 3 January, Barcelona opened their league account for the year with a 0–2 win away against Espanyol at the [[RCDE Stadium|Estadi Cornellà-El Prat]], with goals from Dani Olmo and Robert Lewandowski.

On 7 January, Barcelona reached the final of the [[2026 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] in [[Jeddah]] with a 5–0 win over Athletic Bilbao in the semi-finals, with goals from Ferran Torres, Fermín López, Roony Bardghji, and a brace from Raphinha. Four days later, Barcelona won the Supercopa de España with a 3–2 victory over Real Madrid in the [[2026 Supercopa de España final|final]], with a brace from Raphinha and a goal from Lewandowski.

On 13 January, Barcelona secured the loan of [[Portugal national football_team|Portuguese]] defender [[João Cancelo]] from [[Al Hilal SFC|Al Hilal]] for the remainder of the season.<ref name="Cancelo"/> Two days later, Barcelona advanced to the quarter-finals of the [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] with a 0–2 win away against [[Racing Santander]] at [[Campos de Sport de El Sardinero|El Sardinero]], with goals from Torres and Lamine Yamal. Three days after that, Barcelona were beaten 2–1 away by Real Sociedad at [[Anoeta Stadium|Anoeta]], with Rashford scoring the visitors' only goal.

On 20 January, goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen was loaned to Girona until the end of the campaign.<ref name="Stegen"/> The following day, Barcelona secured a 2–4 win away against [[Slavia Prague]] in the Champions League league phase, with a brace from Fermín and further goals from Olmo and Lewandowski.

On 25 January, Barcelona beat Real Oviedo 3–0 at Camp Nou, with goals from Olmo, Raphinha, and Yamal. The next day, Dro Fernández departed for Paris Saint-Germain for €8.2 million.<ref name="Dro"/>

On 28 January, Barcelona defeated Copenhagen 4–1 at home, with goals from Lewandowski, Yamal, a penalty from Raphinha, and Rashford. Barcelona closed out the month on 31 January with a 1–3 win away against Elche, with goals from Yamal, Torres, and Rashford.

===February===
On 2 February, young defender [[Andrés Cuenca]] was loaned to [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]] for the rest of the season.<ref name="Cuenca"/> The next day, Barcelona advanced to the semi-finals of the Copa del Rey with a 1–2 win away against [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]], with goals from Lamine Yamal and Ronald Araújo.

On 7 February, Barcelona officially withdrew from the [[European Super League]] project.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4446153/fc-barcelona-official-statement |title=FC Barcelona official statement |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=7 February 2026 |access-date=18 September 2026 |archive-date=19 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919032227/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4446153/fc-barcelona-official-statement |url-status=live}}</ref> Later that day, Barcelona beat Mallorca 3–0 at Camp Nou, with goals from Robert Lewandowski, Yamal, and [[Marc Bernal]], the latter netting his first goal for the club. The match also saw [[Tommy Marqués]] make his first-team debut. Two days later, [[Joan Laporta]] and several members of his board resigned from their positions to contest the [[2026 FC Barcelona presidential election|upcoming presidential elections]], with vice-president Rafael Yuste assuming the role of interim president.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4447063/laporta-and-part-of-board-resign-in-order-to-stand-for-re-election |title=Laporta and part of Board resign in order to stand for re-election |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=9 February 2026 |access-date=18 September 2026 |archive-date=19 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919052959/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4447063/laporta-and-part-of-board-resign-in-order-to-stand-for-re-election |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 February, Barcelona were thrashed 4–0 away by Atlético Madrid in the first leg of the Copa del Rey semi-finals, with Eric García opening the scoring with an own goal before further strikes from [[Antoine Griezmann]], [[Ademola Lookman]], and [[Julián Álvarez]]. Four days later, Barcelona were beaten 2–1 away by Girona at [[Estadi Montilivi|Montilivi]], with [[Pau Cubarsí]] scoring the visitors' only goal.

On 22 February, Barcelona returned to winning ways with a 3–0 win over Levante at Camp Nou, with goals from Bernal, [[Frenkie de Jong]], and Fermín López. Barcelona closed out the month on 28 February with a 4–1 home win over Villarreal, with a hat-trick from Yamal and a late goal from Lewandowski.

===March===
On 3 March, Barcelona won the second leg of the Copa del Rey semi-final 3–0 over Atlético Madrid at Camp Nou, with a brace from Marc Bernal and a penalty from Raphinha, but were eliminated 3–4 on aggregate following their first-leg defeat. Four days later, Barcelona won 0–1 away against Athletic Bilbao at [[San Mamés]], with Lamine Yamal scoring the only goal.

On 10 March, Barcelona drew 1–1 away against Newcastle United at [[St James' Park]] in the first leg of the Champions League round of 16, with Lamine Yamal equalising from the penalty spot in stoppage time. [[Xavi Espart]] made his first-team debut in the match. Five days later, Barcelona held [[2026 FC Barcelona presidential election|its presidential elections]], in which Joan Laporta was re-elected as president after defeating challenger Víctor Font.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4470025/joan-laporta-re-elected-as-fc-barcelona-president |title=Joan Laporta re-elected as FC Barcelona President |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=15 March 2026 |access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref> Later that day, Barcelona thrashed Sevilla 5–2 at home, with a hat-trick from Raphinha, including two penalties, and further goals from Dani Olmo and João Cancelo. 

On 18 March, Barcelona routed Newcastle United 7–2 in the second leg to advance 8–3 on aggregate, with braces from Raphinha and Robert Lewandowski, and further goals from Bernal, Yamal, and Fermín López. Barcelona closed out the month on 22 March with a narrow 1–0 win over Rayo Vallecano, with Ronald Araújo scoring the only goal.

===April===
On 4 April, Barcelona won 1–2 away against Atlético Madrid, with goals from Marcus Rashford and Robert Lewandowski. Four days later, Barcelona were beaten 0–2 at home by Atlético Madrid in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals, with Pau Cubarsí sent off before half-time.

On 11 April, Barcelona thrashed Espanyol 4–1 at home, with a brace from Ferran Torres and further goals from Lamine Yamal and Rashford. Three days later, Barcelona won the second leg 1–2 away against Atlético Madrid at the [[Riyadh Air Metropolitano|Metropolitano]], with goals from Yamal and Torres, but were eliminated 3–2 on aggregate after Eric García was sent off late on.

On 22 April, Barcelona edged Celta Vigo 1–0 at Camp Nou, with Yamal converting from the penalty spot. Barcelona closed out the month on 25 April with a 0–2 win away against Getafe at the [[Coliseum Stadium|Coliseum]], with goals from Fermín López and Rashford.

===May===
On 2 May, Barcelona won 1–2 away against Osasuna at [[El Sadar]], with goals from Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

On 10 May, Barcelona beat Real Madrid 2–0 at Camp Nou, with goals from Marcus Rashford and Torres. The win secured Barcelona's [[2025–26 La Liga|29th La Liga title]] and their second in a row, marking the first time in the club's history they had clinched the league via a [[Clásico]] victory. Three days later, Barcelona were beaten 1–0 away by Alavés at [[Mendizorrotza]]. [[Álvaro Cortés]] made his first-team debut in the match. On the same day, Barcelona announced the contract renewal of manager [[Hansi Flick]] through 30 June 2028.

On 17 May, Barcelona beat Real Betis 3–1 at Camp Nou, with a brace from Raphinha and a further goal from João Cancelo. The result saw Barcelona complete the league season with 19 wins from 19 home matches, becoming the first Spanish side in 40 years to sweep all their home fixtures, and the first to do so under the 38-game format.

Barcelona closed out the month on 23 May with a 3–1 defeat away against Valencia at [[Mestalla]], with Lewandowski scoring the visitors' only goal — his last for the club.
